step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram and transcript depict Volkswagen Financial Services' multi-account governance structure using AWS Organizations. AWS Organizations manages baseline stack deployments across various accounts: Workload (EC2), SSO Bifrost (AWS IAM & Fargate hosting Red Hat SSO), Compliance (AWS Config & Inspector), and Auditing (CloudTrail). A SAML connection flows from the SSO Bifrost account to the Workload account to provide federated access for developers.

graph.name: Volkswagen Financial Services Multi-Account Landing Zone Architecture
graph.notes: Shows a centralized landing zone structure managing 1,400+ AWS accounts, with dedicated accounts for Workloads, SSO, Compliance, and Auditing.

nodes.name: AWS Organizations
nodes.notes: Central governance service used to manage baseline stack sets across 1,400+ AWS accounts.

nodes.name: EC2
nodes.notes: Represents production, dev, and staging workloads running across workload accounts.

nodes.name: AWS IAM
nodes.notes: Handles user governance, SAML login, and access recertification.

nodes.name: Fargate
nodes.notes: Runs Red Hat SSO (Bifrost) on ECS/Fargate container cluster.

nodes.name: AWS Config
nodes.notes: Tracks resource changes across all 1,400+ accounts for compliance reporting.

nodes.name: Inspector
nodes.notes: Scans EC2 instances and containers across accounts for vulnerabilities (e.g. Log4j).

nodes.name: CloudTrail
nodes.notes: Centralizes audit logging from all accounts into the dedicated auditing account.

edges.notes: AWS Organizations manages baseline configurations in Workload accounts.
AWS Organizations manages governance policies for identity and access in SSO Bifrost.
AWS Organizations applies compliance baselines and Config rules centrally.
AWS Organizations routes audit logging from all accounts into CloudTrail.
SAML federation authentication allowing developers to log into workload accounts.
